subject: music
title: Chords & Intervals
welcome_lead: How notes stack to make chords and harmony.
meta_desc: KS3 harmony: chords, triads, basic intervals.
final_note: Chords are the colour underneath the melody.

concepts.def: Two or more notes played together.

walkthroughs.body_html: A triad stacks three notes. Pick a note, skip one, pick the next, skip one, pick the next. C-E-G is a C triad. That's a major chord.
Major chords sound bright and happy. Minor chords sound darker and sadder. The difference is just one note moved down by a semitone.
An interval is the gap between two notes. The smallest is a semitone (next key). The biggest common one in basic music is the octave — 8 letter names apart.

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.

mcqs.q: What is a balanced antecedent-consequent phrase?
options: Two phrases of equal length where the first sounds open (question) and the second resolves (answer).
A long melody with no breaks.
Any two phrases of similar style.
